decisions.reason: Reassigning 5V_EN from GPIO3 to GPIO5 does not change the standalone USB-powered 3.3V supply or its source-selection behavior.
The GPIO reassignment does not change the AXP2101 battery and USB power-path topology.
The interboard connector continues to carry the signal named 5V_EN; changing the MCU GPIO driving that signal does not alter the connector pinout.
A complete same-message MODIFY already records 5V_EN as GPIO5, the SCL0 and SPI_MOSI reassignments, and the unexposed module GPIOs.
The 5V_EN GPIO reassignment does not affect the battery connector's series, pinout, or mounting type.
The LED supply remains 5V and still requires data-level shifting; the GPIO used to control the shared 5V rail does not change those requirements.
This Requirement explicitly uses the 5V_EN control GPIO to cut LED power, so reassigning 5V_EN necessarily changes its control_gpio from GPIO3 to GPIO5.

source_message.speaker: client
source_message.text: Sorry, GPIO3 was from my original ESP32 design — mistake on my side. For 5V_EN you can use GPIO5. Also I realized GPIO22, 23, 25, 27 are not exposed on the WROOM-1 module, so I need to reassign SCL0 (GPIO22→38), SPI MOSI (GPIO23→26). I'll update the docs and send you the full updated GPIO table.

decisions.reason: The GPIO reassignment has no effect on battery connector placement, orientation, spacing, or mounting-hole clearance.
The source decision changes an MCU signal assignment and does not change component availability or sourcing policy.
The 5V_EN GPIO reassignment does not alter the power board's mechanical layout, enclosure fit, connectors, or layer count.
The sensor board's role of providing sensor connectors remains unchanged by the MCU GPIO reassignment.
The source decision does not specify any BOM entry, component value, part number, or assembly-documentation change.
